maxWords: How many words of the input text are used when scoring patterns.
Words after this limit are ignored. The default 256 is enough for a short article or a long social post.
Raise it only if you routinely paste longer text and need those later words to affect the pattern choice.
maxSlugLength: Maximum length of the slug, in characters.
The slug is cut on a word boundary so it never ends mid-word. The title is never truncated.
joiner: The word placed only before the last keyword in a list.
With joiner "and", three keywords become baked-beans-toast-and-tea. An empty joiner gives plain hyphens: baked-beans-toast-tea.
Change this for another language, or clear it for a tighter slug. Variants such as "and the" are mixed in via joinerVariants.
joinerVariants: Extra joiner phrases mixed with the main joiner before the last keyword.
English default includes "and the", so titles can read Potatoes and the John Lloyd Experience as well as Potatoes and Toast.
Used joinerVariantFactor of the time when the list has two or more keywords.
joinerVariantFactor: Chance, from 0 to 1, of using a joiner variant instead of the main joiner.
At 0, only the main joiner is used. At 1, a variant is always chosen when the list is non-empty.
pluralFactor: Chance, from 0 to 1, that an eligible keyword is made plural in the slug and the title.
A keyword is eligible when its last letter is not s and not a vowel (a, e, i, o, u or y). "baked beans" and "tea" stay as written. "toast" can become "toasts".
At 0, nothing is pluralized. At 1, every eligible keyword is. Each keyword is rolled on its own, and the same input and seed always roll the same way. The default 0.3 is about a 30% chance.
keywordWeight: How strongly keywords count when scoring patterns.
Keywords that also appear as triggers pull the match toward those patterns. Higher values make that pull stronger.
Leave the default unless a keyword is also a trigger and you want to dial that effect up or down.
minScore: A pattern must score strictly above this to be a candidate.
At 0 (the default), any positive score can win. Raise it to ignore weak matches and fall back to generic patterns more often.
patternSpread: How close to the best score a pattern must be to stay in the running, from 0 to 1.
At 0.2, a pattern needs at least 20% of the best score. At 1, only the single best pattern can be chosen.
Lower it for more variety across patterns; raise it when you want the closest match to dominate.
sharedFactor: The chance, from 0 to 1, of using a shared template instead of the chosen pattern's own.
Shared templates work with any pattern. At 0 they are never used; at 1 they are preferred whenever the list is non-empty.
Raise it for more generic, pattern-independent titles.
connectFactor: When two or more keywords are given, the chance of using a connecting template that joins or compares them.
At 0, connecting titles are off. At 1, they are always preferred when available.
quirks: Turns quirks mode on or off.
When on, there is a quirk-factor chance of using quirky templates (adjectives, playful endings) and of adding quirky numbers to {n}.
numbers: The plain values {n} picks from. Each entry is a string: a digit or a word.
The English defaults are 2, 3, 5, two, three and five. Always in the pool, quirks or not.
Add or remove entries to change what can appear. A word is title-cased in the title and kept as written in the slug.
quirkyNumbers: Extra {n} values appended only when quirks mode is on and the quirk-factor roll hits.
A number or a short phrase is fine ("A bunch"). It is title-cased in the title and hyphenated in the slug.
With quirks off, or when the roll stays plain, these entries are not used. Add or remove them to change what can appear on a quirky roll.
quirkFactor: When quirks mode is on, the chance, from 0 to 1, of a quirky result instead of a plain one.

That chance picks a quirky template when one is available, and it adds the quirky numbers to the {n} pool. At 1, the quirky path is always taken. At 0, quirks mode can be on and every title still stays plain, numbers included. It does nothing while quirks mode is off.
The factor slider next to Quirks on the tester overrides this for that one run.
